val: We cannot allow any disruption to the war effort, so we are passing new legislation to enforce total compliance with government aims. This will protect the flow of resources and allow us to focus political energy where it is needed.
It is time to mobilize more of the South African population demi upaya perang. Women can be brought into the factories at lower cost, as well.
South Africa lags behind other Dominions in science and technology, so establishing the Council for Scientific and Industrial Research in Pretoria has become a pressing matter for the government.

The Cape remains an important sea route for many nations, and is the gateway to the South African heartland. Expansion of the garrison's coastal defenses and artillery should be at the top of our to-do list.

Historically, we have been able to press some of our Colored population into service to defend South Africa. This is not popular with everyone in the country, but it will free white South Africans to serve overseas.
Though we reconstituted the Cape Corps as a mostly non-combatant force, the threat of invasion means we must give the Corps greater resources, training and access to weapons.

Poor rural Afrikaners have flooded into the cities seeking work for the last few years, and we’ve done little to help them. Until now. Industrialization and government protection of their access to work will help this population.
Work stoppages and labor disruption is unpatriotic in times of crisis. Strikes are hereby declared illegal, and the government will force people back to work.
We have had a mandate over the former German colony of South-West Africa since the last war ended. It is vital that we live up to our duty to secure and improve the major city of Windhoek.
The Commonwealth nations are pooling their resources and experience to facilitate and accelerate the training of pilots and air crew.
The war in North Africa requires specialized equipment and as our forces could be called to serve on that front, the provision and supply of that equipment will become an important logistical matter.

The Fascist pro-German Ossewabrandwag (OB) has a paramilitary wing modeled on similar European groups. They are disrupting government efforts to recruit troops and pursue a secure and united war policy. The Stormjaers must be broken up.
The Union of South Africa neighbors a number of British colonies that could be left to our administration. We should also do what we can to permanently secure our Mandate over South-West Africa.

To further guarantee work for the Afrikaner population, we must limit the settlement of Black South Africans within the cities. Only those with a long history in the municipality will have residency rights.
We should push harder to legally separate our different ethnic populations to promote the power and unity of our ruling class.

The replacement of the Cape route by the Suez, as well as the formative experience of the Boer War have helped create a South African identity distinct from that of our Dominion allies. We should distance ourselves from the King, and forge our own path.

The Afrikaner Broederbond has been agitating for a greater voice for the Afrikaner people and stronger separation of the races. The memory of British policy in the Boer War is still strong, and the Broederbond can help create a new South Africa.
The Fascist Ossewabrandwag paramilitary should be used as a bulwark against foreign agitation and domestic uprisings that target our ruling class.

A century ago, our Afrikaner ancestors separated from the rising British colonial power and built their own Boer nation in the northeast. Their hardy spirit still represents the best of South African virtue.
A monument to the Voortrekkers who undertook the Great Trek will strengthen national spirit and unity in these troubling times.
As a former German colony, it is only appropriate that we encourage the growth of German political ideas in South-West Africa.

The German government has long seen South Africa as fertile ground for greater influence, dating back to the last century. Our future lies with the Reich, not the Empire, so let's move forward with the plan to overthrow the current government.
The former Boer territory of Transvaal and other regions rightfully belong to the free heirs of that enterprising people.
In 1838, a wagon laager of Boer settlers held off tens of thousands of Zulu warriors, dealing a crippling blow to Zulu power in the Natal. This was surely a divine sign of the rightness of our cause.
German scientists are among the best in the world and have much to share with us.
The Axis powers have an energy and ideology that can help South Africa establish its place in the world. We should give them our full diplomatic support.
South Africa should have a king, and fortunately there is a Windsor that no one is using right now. The former Edward VIII, Duke of Windsor, can sit on our throne.
We are a country of miners and farmers. The working people of South Africa are the only true representation of the national will.
Fascism is on the rise in Europe, and we can stop it in Spain - or at least slow its spread. Men and material should be sent to support the Republican cause.
Racial discrimination is contrary to the values of popular revolution in South Africa. Blacks should be restored to the general voting rolls and given political rights.
Down with the Royal Family! This symbolic gesture will publicly declare our breach from the foreign throne.
The Soviet Union has been in the forefront of the crusade for the workers and against Fascism. We shall join their mighty alliance.
The only way for the workers to triumph is to unite the entire globe in a single effort. The Revolution must be universal and, therefore, it must be exported.
If we are to improve the lot of workers in our nation, we must start with ensuring that all workers are treated equal, regardless of their color of skin.

The South African Railways company needs to be expanded. Bands of youth can be trained there, and given the necessary skills to both work in the country and serve overseas.
South Africa's mineral wealth is legendary, and we’ve only just begun to tap its deep reserves of gold, chromium and platinum.

It is important that South Africa stay up to date with the latest in engineering techniques. Even though our industrial base is small, we should invest in heavy machinery and engineering to quickly catch up to our peers.
Much of South Africa remains rural and undeveloped. More roads and railroads can bring the natural wealth of the country to its hungry ports.
South Africa is safe from invasion by any foreign power, but also remote from its allies. It is vital that it develop its own arms industry so that the Union is never undefended.
We have the coal and iron. Now we have the reason. Expansion of the Iscor steel works in Pretoria will provide the country with the heavy steel plating necessary for modern weapons.
The existing steel works in Pretoria has focused on heavy plate. With some machine tools, however, we can convert some of the factory into a center for small arms production.
The Rand Mines are some of the deepest gold mines in the world - and so even with 19th-century technology. We are capable of so much more now. Dig deep! And greedily, even.

Pretoria's University of South Africa is one of the best universities on the continent - in the southern hemisphere, even. By investing in it, we can grow our own local talent instead of sending our young people overseas.
Atomic weapons will be the greatest military breakthrough since gunpowder, not to mention the peaceful uses of this power if we can harness the atom. Gather our top scientists to study this.

Now that South Africa is fully a sovereign nation we are no longer receiving access to advanced prototypes and blueprints like we previously did. Kita harus ensure that we always stay ahead of our enemies, and do not fall behind in technology.

The British showed us the advantage of sharing scientific progress between close allies. Our whole faction will be able to conduct wartime R&D more efficiently if we take the steps necessary to coordinate this.
South Africa is full of young, unemployed men who need to find something useful to do. The Special Service Battalion will instill some much-needed discipline and organization.

South Africa's troops will be fighting in varied climates, and we are fortunate that the Lee-Enfield rifle is easily customized. The .303 cartridge has been modified a number of times by other countries to suit their needs.
The Q Services Corps will be the centralized authority responsible for the logistics and supply of the permanent army. It will handle the distribution of oil, rations, ammo and uniforms.
South Africa should have a military academy modeled on the lines of West Point in the United States. This will give us a professional officer corps loyal to the Union.
The artillery corps was unified in 1934. Now the time has come to increase its size and capacity.
The South African Engineer Corps has barely 600 men in uniform. This is unacceptable in a modern army. We need more men and more training for this crucial task.
We cannot neglect the supply of support equipment needed for our army. Guns and tanks are well and good, but we need uniforms, radios, repair kits and more.
South Africa needs a home-grown commando squad to handle those difficult jobs in hard-to-reach places.
Motorized and mechanized war is upon us. The Great Trek of the future will be guided by tracked and wheeled vehicles.
Tanks have come a long way from the sluggish beasts of the last war. Our research and training cannot fall behind that of our enemies - or our friends.
We have developed a Five-Year Plan for the modernization and expansion of the South African air force. The government must publicly commit to not fall behind this schedule.
The Hawker Hartbees we have are not the most advanced fighters in the world, but we will make do. Improved mechanics and training will get the most out of these biplanes.
The Bristol Blenheim has been a serviceable light bomber for the RAF, and for the Dominions. But it may be time to find something sturdier, with a longer range.
The \"Cab-Rank\" Technique has a series of bombers strike a target one at a time, in a long row. This maintains pressure on the enemy, but takes a great amount of skill.
The desert skies are clear, and the heat and sand mean special attention to the mechanics of our aircraft. There are valuable skills to be learned in this unforgiving environment.
If the Suez should fall, the Cape will again be the gateway to the East. Defend it at all costs.

Too often our experienced pilots move on to the RAF instead of staying with our own force. The RAF has better opportunities for advancement and combat. But we should endeavor to keep our trained pilots close to home where they can inspire and educate other South Africans.
The Seaward Defense Force has served as our navy for two decades. Its funding should be increased.
The last war showed the importance of convoys and escorts. South Africa lies on a major trade route and should make sure that the goods get through to their destination.
The last war showed the importance of convoys and escorts. South Africa lies on a major trade route and is ideally situated to intercept and destroy enemy shipping.
Simon's Town on the Cape has been the most important naval base in southern Africa since the 1790s. It should be refitted and expanded to accommodate more and larger vessels.
Submarines threaten the ships that pass through the Cape of Good Hope. Kita harus find and destroy them.
Enemy trade convoys continue to use the pass through the Cape of Good Hope. Kita akan strike them from below.
With miles of coastline, South Africa is fit to train its soldiers in amphibious war. This is one of the most difficult of skills, but our boys can handle it.
The Cape Garrison guns must be upgraded and increased to protect the Cape from enemy attack.
